rules: book value is at least salvage value (tolerance 0.01), because the charge is capped at the salvage floor
book value is at most original cost, because depreciation is never negative
book value is non-negative when cost and salvage are non-negative
if elapsed years is 0, book value equals cost
with life >= 2 and years >= 1 and cost > salvage, book value is strictly below cost, because at least some depreciation is charged

functions: Compute the book value after a given number of elapsed years under double-declining-balance depreciation that never falls below salvage value.
Iterate double-declining-balance yearly depreciation with a salvage-value floor from the original cost for the elapsed years and return the unrounded book value.
Parse a monetary amount in dollars from raw text, handling currency sign, thousands separators and scale words such as k, thousand, million, bn and billion.
Parse a whole number of years or a useful life from raw text, handling digits and number words.

rules: Payment must be positive when principal is positive: a loan with positive principal requires positive payments.

Total interest is at most simple interest on the full principal over the whole term, plus a rounding allowance of half a cent per payment. Amortizing reduces the balance over time, so interest cannot exceed that.
Payment times number of payments minus principal equals total interest, within 0.01 per payment for rounding. This is how the outputs are defined.
Payment is at least principal divided by the number of payments, within a cent. Even at 0% the payments must repay the principal.
Payment is at most principal times (1 + periodic rate). Otherwise the first payment would exceed the whole balance plus its interest.

functions: Compute the growth factor (1+r)^n and the unrounded level periodic annuity payment from principal, periodic rate and number of payments, treating a zero rate as principal divided by number of payments.
Compute the periodic interest rate (annual rate divided by periods per year) and the total number of payments (periods per year times term in years).
Determine the number of compounding periods per year from a frequency description such as monthly, quarterly, semiannual, annual, weekly, biweekly or daily.
Parse a loan term from raw text (digits or number words, in years or months) into a term in years and a term in months.
Parse a money amount from raw text with currency symbols, separators and scale suffixes into an exact Decimal dollar amount.
Parse a percentage rate from raw text such as '7.5%' or '7.5 percent' into an exact Decimal annual rate as a fraction.
Round the periodic payment to the cent with half-up rounding and compute total interest as the rounded payment times the number of payments minus the principal.
Solve a fixed-rate amortizing loan: compute the level periodic payment and the total interest paid over the term, from the principal, the annual nominal rate, the compounding frequency and the term.
